  - bash
  - config
user-invocable: true
disable-model-invocation: false
---

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:
  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to
  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands
  between your edit and that.
- **YAML syntax errors remain silent at RUNTIME** (an unparseable file falls
  back to defaults) — `check` is the only place they ar…

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Closes #1636
### Root Cause
When auto-compaction fired, `formatCompactionReport` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart`) unconditionally rendered the full detail block — the `records:` line plus the entire internal checkpoint summary in a fenced block — and the CLI hooks wrote it to the console on every fold. The headless log face additionally streamed every summarizer delta (the whole summary text) live. No config key gated any of it (`tui:` only knew `theme`/`classic`/`statusLine`).

### Fix
- `formatCompactionReport` gained `details` (default `false`): the default report is ONE marker line — `● auto-compacted · engine: N → M tokens (F freed · P%)`.
- New config key `tui.showCompactionDetails` (default `false`; strict-parsed, `fa config set`-writable, persisted only when true): `true` restores the full block and the headless live delta stream. The manual `/compact` always renders the full block (it IS the on-demand expansion).
- Liveness with details hidden is unchanged: the gh-1430 `… reasoning Ns` line already covers the compaction window on line-mode/headless faces.
- Nothing is lost by default — the summary stays in the session file, reachable via `compact_expand`.
- Files: `agent_cli_compaction.dart`, `tui_status_line.dart`, `cli_config.dart`, `agent_cli_config.dart`, `config_service.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `cli_help.dart`, `prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md`.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/compaction_report_test.dart`: new `gh-1636 one-line default` group (marker line, no checkpoint text; `details: true` keeps the full block).
- `test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart`: default headless log face is summary-free (no delta echo, one marker line, continuation intact); the gh-1433 E4 dim thinking stream is pinned under the opt-in.
- `test/cli/structured_compaction_observability_test.dart`: one receipt per fold on default; counters-match-session pinned under the opt-in.
- `test/cli/tui_status_line_test.dart` + `test/config/config_service_test.dart`: key parse/round-trip/strict-validation + `fa config set` end-to-end.
- Fixture repair the fix exposed: `agent_cli_over_window_windowed_resume_test` passed on a false positive — the answer turn was consumed as the post-run summary and matched the assertion only through the printed summary fence (the continuation itself crashed with an exhausted-script RangeError, at the base commit too). The script now carries explicit filler turns for every compaction-pipeline request, so the assertion verifies the real continuation answer.
- Full suite (`test/cli`, `test/compaction`, `test/config`): all green.

### Notes
- Deliberate behavior change: the gh-1433 E4 "no silent windows" headless delta stream and the issue #438 stderr counter lines are now opt-in (`tui.showCompactionDetails: true`); the receipt-per-fold contract (one `● auto-compacted` line per fold, honest token numbers) is unchanged.
- Related-but-different issues untouched: #653 (stale badge), #286, #1425.

title: "dart-test runner-zone landmine: `unawaited(future.catchError(handler))` on a `Future<T>` that ALSO has a `.then(onValue, onError:)` listener can fail under the `dart test` runner zone with \"The error handler of Future.catchError must return a value of the future's type\" — even though the handler runs and returns a valid T (root-zone scripts do NOT reproduce it; the delivery path differs under the runner's StackZoneSpecification). Seen in gh-1054's `_supervisedAttempt` zombie guard (`unawaited(inner.catchError((_) => ToolExecutionResult.text('')))`) the first time a supervised executor actually ERRORED post-cancel; every prior test used never-completing zombies so the guard never fired. Fix: the guard was redundant — the `.then(onValue, onError:)` waiter registered right after already consumes the error; deleting the catchError removed the failure for all 18 supervisor tests. Rule: never attach a second (unawaited) catchError to a future that already has a then-error listener; if a runner-only catchError-type error appears, look for the redundant guard first."

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:
  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to
  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands
  between your edit and that.
- **YAML syntax errors remain silent at RUNTIME** (an unparseable file falls
  back to defaults) — `check` is the only place they ar…

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

## PR Description

Closes #1636
### Root Cause
When auto-compaction fired, `formatCompactionReport` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart`) unconditionally rendered the full detail block — the `records:` line plus the entire internal checkpoint summary in a fenced block — and the CLI hooks wrote it to the console on every fold. The headless log face additionally streamed every summarizer delta (the whole summary text) live. No config key gated any of it (`tui:` only knew `theme`/`classic`/`statusLine`).

### Fix
- `formatCompactionReport` gained `details` (default `false`): the default report is ONE marker line — `● auto-compacted · engine: N → M tokens (F freed · P%)`.
- New config key `tui.showCompactionDetails` (default `false`; strict-parsed, `fa config set`-writable, persisted only when true): `true` restores the full block and the headless live delta stream. The manual `/compact` always renders the full block (it IS the on-demand expansion).
- Liveness with details hidden is unchanged: the gh-1430 `… reasoning Ns` line already covers the compaction window on line-mode/headless faces.
- Nothing is lost by default — the summary stays in the session file, reachable via `compact_expand`.
- Files: `agent_cli_compaction.dart`, `tui_status_line.dart`, `cli_config.dart`, `agent_cli_config.dart`, `config_service.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `cli_help.dart`, `prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md`.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/compaction_report_test.dart`: new `gh-1636 one-line default` group (marker line, no checkpoint text; `details: true` keeps the full block).
- `test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart`: default headless log face is summary-free (no delta echo, one marker line, continuation intact); the gh-1433 E4 dim thinking stream is pinned under the opt-in.
- `test/cli/structured_compaction_observability_test.dart`: one receipt per fold on default; counters-match-session pinned under the opt-in.
- `test/cli/tui_status_line_test.dart` + `test/config/config_service_test.dart`: key parse/round-trip/strict-validation + `fa config set` end-to-end.
- Fixture repair the fix exposed: `agent_cli_over_window_windowed_resume_test` passed on a false positive — the answer turn was consumed as the post-run summary and matched the assertion only through the printed summary fence (the continuation itself crashed with an exhausted-script RangeError, at the base commit too). The script now carries explicit filler turns for every compaction-pipeline request, so the assertion verifies the real continuation answer.
- Full suite (`test/cli`, `test/compaction`, `test/config`): all green.

### Notes
- Deliberate behavior change: the gh-1433 E4 "no silent windows" headless delta stream and the issue #438 stderr counter lines are now opt-in (`tui.showCompactionDetails: true`); the receipt-per-fold contract (one `● auto-compacted` line per fold, honest token numbers) is unchanged.
- Related-but-different issues untouched: #653 (stale badge), #286, #1425.

title: "dart-test runner-zone landmine: `unawaited(future.catchError(handler))` on a `Future<T>` that ALSO has a `.then(onValue, onError:)` listener can fail under the `dart test` runner zone with \"The error handler of Future.catchError must return a value of the future's type\" — even though the handler runs and returns a valid T (root-zone scripts do NOT reproduce it; the delivery path differs under the runner's StackZoneSpecification). Seen in gh-1054's `_supervisedAttempt` zombie guard (`unawaited(inner.catchError((_) => ToolExecutionResult.text('')))`) the first time a supervised executor actually ERRORED post-cancel; every prior test used never-completing zombies so the guard never fired. Fix: the guard was redundant — the `.then(onValue, onError:)` waiter registered right after already consumes the error; deleting the catchError removed the failure for all 18 supervisor tests. Rule: never attach a second (unawaited) catchError to a future that already has a then-error listener; if a runner-only catchError-type error appears, look for the redundant guard first."

# Note: n_0979_f457

dart-test runner-zone landmine: `unawaited(future.catchError(handler))` on a `Future<T>` that ALSO has a `.then(onValue, onError:)` listener can fail under the `dart test` runner zone with "The error handler of Future.catchError must return a value of the future's type" — even though the handler runs and returns a valid T (root-zone scripts do NOT reproduce it; the delivery path differs under the runner's StackZoneSpecification). Seen in gh-1054's `_supervisedAttempt` zombie guard (`unawaited(inner.catchError((_) => ToolExecutionResult.text('')))`) the first time a supervised executor actually ERRORED post-cancel; every prior test used never-completing zombies so the guard never fired. Fix: the guard was redundant — the `.then(onValue, onError:)` waiter registered right after already consumes the error; deleting the catchError removed the failure for all 18 supervisor tests. Rule: never attach a second (unawaited) catchError to a future that already has a then-error listener; if a runner-only catchError-type error appears, look for the redundant guard first.

- My 3 threads (`PRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uu82N`, `PRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uu85b`, `PRT_kwDOTXdlLc6uu88t`) were all addressed by the rework commits and resolved (3 resolved threads excluded).
- The rework head `98f4d437f9` went through validation CI and it went RED — "Core tests (shard 3/4)" exit 255 — with a coverage/VM-service load crash on `test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart` (a file this PR never touches). The bot says "red 1/3" — after 3 reds on the same head, validation waits for a NEW head. This is round 2 red #1.
- The discussion shows the machine re-armed rework, and now I'm re-reviewing.

Now the critical question for THIS re-review: is the red CI attributable to the PR's code?

Evidence for "infra flake, not PR code":
1. The failure is a **load** failure: "Failed to load test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart: streamListen: (-32000) Service connection disposed" + "Connection closed before test suite loaded", inside `package:coverage` `_getAllCoverage` — the coverage collector's VM service died. The stack is entirely in test_core/coverage/vm_service infra.
2. `sessions_picker_test.dart` is NOT touched by this PR (not in the 17 files).
3. Every actual test in the shard's log tail is ✅; no assertion failures.
4. `dart-lang/test`'s own message: "This is an unexpected error. Please file an issue at http://github.com/dart-lang/test".

But before concluding, let me verify:
1. `sessions_picker_test.dart` loads and passes locally on this head (it might be affected by the MERGE from main — the branch merged main 3f382ada51; if main introduced something sessions_picker depends on... but CI on main was green presumably).
2. Check the rework diff itself for correctness (the delegation to parseTuiSection from config_service — is tui_status_line.dart pure Dart? The rework claims verified. Let me verify: does tui_status_line.dart (or its transitive imports) use dart:io? lib/ is pure Dart by policy — tui_status_line is in lib/src/cli/, and cli files CAN import dart:io only via lib/io.dart. Since lib/ must compile for web, and tui_status_line.dart is part of lib/, it can't import dart:io directly. But its TRANSITIVE closure might pull dart:io via some import. If it did, config_service.dart (pure, used by web?) would break the web build — CI has a web compile stage? The failed check is "Core tests shard 3/4" only; analyze stage passed. Let me verify purity quickly.
3. Re-run the prompts_sync + config + tui tests on this head to confirm the fixes.
4. Fresh full diff review (the rework commits + merge from main). The merge brought main's changes into the branch — the diff origin/main...HEAD is still the PR surface (merge-base based, so merged-in main changes don't appear as PR changes... actually with a merge commit, `git diff origin/main...HEAD` = diff from merge-base to HEAD, which includes main's changes brought in by the merge PLUS the PR changes. Hmm — no: merge-base of origin/main and HEAD after merging main INTO the branch: the merge-base is the OLD main head (before new main commits)... wait, if the branch merged the CURRENT main, then origin/main might have advanced since? Let me check: `git merge-base origin/main HEAD`. If the merge consumed all of main, the merge-base == origin/main tip, and the diff shows only the PR's own changes. Good.
5. Check scope of rework commits — they match my threads exactly (no scope creep).

Then the verdict question: red CI on head. Per F7 + verdict rules → include as 🚨 BLOCKING → REQUEST_CHANGES. The rework round will re-run CI (the bot's "red 1/3 ... after 3 reds waits for NEW head" — a re-review verdict of REQUEST_CHANGES with blocking:1 arms another rework; the rework will presumably just re-run/re-trigger validation).

Hmm, wait. Is REQUEST_CHANGES the right call for an infra flake? Let me re-read the anti-patterns:
- ❌ REQUEST_CHANGES because re-review surfaced new suggestion nits — a cycle with ONLY suggestion findings must APPROVE.
- ❌ REQUEST_CHANGES while blocking=0.
- Nothing says "flake → approve". And F7 says CI failures = BLOCKING. The verdict table: "Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) → REQUEST_CHANGES — or BLOCK for security/data loss".

A red validation gate on the head is by-the-book BLOCKING. The rework loop machine needs the PR to have a green head to merge; red CI physically blocks the merge (bot aborted). If I APPROVE with a red head, the machine might merge on red — bad. If I REQUEST_CHANGES with the CI failure as the blocking finding, rework re-runs validation; next run is likely green (flake).

But also consider: maybe I should verify the flake hypothesis more rigorously so the rework doesn't thrash. Options:
1. Run `dart test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart` locally on this head — if green locally, supports flake.
2. Check the log for whether the shard was under memory pressure (OOM could kill the VM service). Coverage runs are heavy (that's why there are 4 shards). 

Also — is there any chance the rework code (config_service importing tui_status_line) introduced a LOAD-TIME crash in that shard? A load crash from a cyclic import or a static initializer would be deterministic and would hit EVERY shard that loads config_service... config_service is used by lots of tests across shards; only shard 3/4 failed and only at the END of the run (11:35:00, after most tests passed). Also the load failure happened at 11:35:00 — the shard was nearly done (sessions_picker is alphabetically late in test/cli). The failure is in the coverage GATHER phase at suite load — classic resource exhaustion / VM service death. Also note: the first failure line "getVM: (-32000) Service connection disposed" happened during `VmService.streamListen` at LOAD time of sessions_picker_test — the VM service connection was already dead, then coverage gather also failed. This smells like the VM/DDS connection died mid-run (OOM or timeout), then everything after failed.

Hmm — one more angle: did the PREVIOUS run on the ORIGINAL head (6b669060e — which the bot quotes as red head) also fail the same way? The bot message says "🔴 red head 6b669060e... red 1/3". Wait — 6b669060e was the ORIGINAL head ("gh-1636 WIP auto-save 2026-10-21T10-29-00" — the head I reviewed in round 1). Its validation CI also went red — that was the prompts_sync failure presumably (my BLOCKING). Hmm, actually the bot line says "Validation CI went red on the head — merge aborted, rework re-queued ... 🔴 red head 6b669060e ... red 1/3 (after 3 reds on the same head, validation waits for a NEW head)". So on the OLD head 6b669, red count 1/3 (the prompts_sync red). Then rework produced new head 98f4d437, and ITS validation run failed on shard 3/4 (the coverage crash). The ci_failures.md says "1 check(s) failed on commit `98f4d437`".

So this round: the ONLY blocking-class item is the red validation gate on the new head, and the failing check is an infra-class load/coverage crash in a file the PR doesn't touch.

Decision per the machine protocol: the gate is red → BLOCKING finding → REQUEST_CHANGES (blocking: 1). I'll phrase the thread precisely: not a code regression, it's the coverage/VM-service flake class; the fix action is a validation re-run (new CI run on the same head or a no-op re-push); note the "red 1/3" counter and that all PR-touched suites are green locally on this head. Actually — hmm, REQUEST_CHANGES arms a REWORK round (the author agent does another pass). The rework agent will read my thread: "CI red — infra flake class — re-run validation / push new head" — that's exactly the right instruction.

Alternatively APPROVE — but that would let the machine treat the head as approved with a red validation run. The bot explicitly aborted the merge on red. And the protocol's letter (F7, verdict table) says failing gate = BLOCKING = REQUEST_CHANGES. I'll follow the letter.

Before finalizing, due diligence:
1. Verify rework diffs (read them fully).
2. Verify prompts.g.dart regenerated + gen check green + prompts_sync green on THIS head.
3. Verify config_service delegation compiles + purity (no dart:io in closure) + new tests pass.
4. Verify _tuiBoolFlag dedupe + tests.
5. Run sessions_picker_test.dart locally to support the flake classification.…

when_to_use: Reconfiguring fa itself — settings, provider, models, memory,
  tools, cubes, MCP, redaction, skills access, themes/TUI appearance — on
  any host (CLI headless, REPL, app), by editing the YAML config the CLI
  persists (themes also via ~/.fah/themes/*.json), never by guessing keys.
argument-hint: "[what to configure, e.g. 'point project memory at ./memory']"
allowed-tools:

  - write
  - edit

  - bash
  - config
user-invocable: true
disable-model-invocation: false

# fa self-configuration

You are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the
CLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin
editors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent
keys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.

## Hard rules

1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict
   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can
   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,
   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on
   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can
   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.
2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES
   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the
   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.
3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for
   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.
4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool's `check` op (or
   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A
   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.
5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which
   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.

## Config layout and precedence

| File | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |
| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |
| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |
| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |
| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |
| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |

Project precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,
`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file
(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,
`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the
same section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from
the user file only.

Project sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws
`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is
created with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind
(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).

## Workflow

1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.
2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two
   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).
3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before
   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to
   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:
   removing a key.
4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).
5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made
   the same change.

## The config tool

The primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —
because it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the
same core the human CLI verbs wrap:

| op | args | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |
| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |
| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |
| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |

`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change
applies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`
defaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal
when absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`
to override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects
unknown top-level keys instead of writing them.
`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an
array or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`
provider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key
`customProviders`, value
`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.
`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round
trip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one
entry, get first and re-set the extended list.
`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer
`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and
never suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP
server (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and
iOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via
`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)
the global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project
sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.

Human/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):
`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,
`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and
`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —
the one verb without a config-file write).

## Verification

`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the
REAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory
final step of every edit:

- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):
  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,
  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,
  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming
  file+section.
- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;
  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.
- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:
  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to
  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands
  between your edit and that.
- **YAML syntax errors remain silent at RUNTIME** (an unparseable file falls
  back to defaults) — `check` is the only place they ar…

Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Closes #1636
### Root Cause
When auto-compaction fired, `formatCompactionReport` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart`) unconditionally rendered the full detail block — the `records:` line plus the entire internal checkpoint summary in a fenced block — and the CLI hooks wrote it to the console on every fold. The headless log face additionally streamed every summarizer delta (the whole summary text) live. No config key gated any of it (`tui:` only knew `theme`/`classic`/`statusLine`).

### Fix
- `formatCompactionReport` gained `details` (default `false`): the default report is ONE marker line — `● auto-compacted · engine: N → M tokens (F freed · P%)`.
- New config key `tui.showCompactionDetails` (default `false`; strict-parsed, `fa config set`-writable, persisted only when true): `true` restores the full block and the headless live delta stream. The manual `/compact` always renders the full block (it IS the on-demand expansion).
- Liveness with details hidden is unchanged: the gh-1430 `… reasoning Ns` line already covers the compaction window on line-mode/headless faces.
- Nothing is lost by default — the summary stays in the session file, reachable via `compact_expand`.
- Files: `agent_cli_compaction.dart`, `tui_status_line.dart`, `cli_config.dart`, `agent_cli_config.dart`, `config_service.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `cli_help.dart`, `prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md`.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/compaction_report_test.dart`: new `gh-1636 one-line default` group (marker line, no checkpoint text; `details: true` keeps the full block).
- `test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart`: default headless log face is summary-free (no delta echo, one marker line, continuation intact); the gh-1433 E4 dim thinking stream is pinned under the opt-in.
- `test/cli/structured_compaction_observability_test.dart`: one receipt per fold on default; counters-match-session pinned under the opt-in.
- `test/cli/tui_status_line_test.dart` + `test/config/config_service_test.dart`: key parse/round-trip/strict-validation + `fa config set` end-to-end.
- Fixture repair the fix exposed: `agent_cli_over_window_windowed_resume_test` passed on a false positive — the answer turn was consumed as the post-run summary and matched the assertion only through the printed summary fence (the continuation itself crashed with an exhausted-script RangeError, at the base commit too). The script now carries explicit filler turns for every compaction-pipeline request, so the assertion verifies the real continuation answer.
- Full suite (`test/cli`, `test/compaction`, `test/config`): all green.

### Notes
- Deliberate behavior change: the gh-1433 E4 "no silent windows" headless delta stream and the issue #438 stderr counter lines are now opt-in (`tui.showCompactionDetails: true`); the receipt-per-fold contract (one `● auto-compacted` line per fold, honest token numbers) is unchanged.
- Related-but-different issues untouched: #653 (stale badge), #286, #1425.

Fix: the guard was redundant — the `.then(onValue, onError:)` waiter registered right after already consumes the error; deleting the catchError removed the failure for all 18 supervisor tests. Rule: never attach a second (unawaited) catchError to a future that already has a then-error listener; if a runner-only catchError-type error appears, look for the redundant guard first."
